title: Tetrazine Amino Acid Encoding for Rapid and Complete Protein Bioconjugation
author: Alex J. Eddins

steps.title: Prepare LB/agar plates with antibiotics
steps.instruction: Make LB/agar (0.5 L) with 1 % tryptone, 0.5 % yeast extract, 1 % NaCl, 1.5 % agar, autoclave, cool to ~55 °C, add antibiotics, pour plates, solidify and label.

substeps.instruction: Mix 5 g tryptone, 2.5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 7.5 g agar in ~450 mL water; bring to 500 mL with water.
Autoclave on standard liquid setting.
Cool to ~55 °C (molten agar still liquid).

For BL21(DE3) plates add 50 µL spectinomycin stock (100 µg/mL final) and 50 µL kanamycin stock (50 µg/mL final). For B95(DE3) plates add 25 µL of each stock (final 50 µg/mL spectinomycin, 25 µg/mL kanamycin).
Swirl gently, pour ~15–20 mL into each 100 mm plate, let solidify with lid ajar for ~30 min, then label (e.g., “pAJE3 + pET28‑sfGFP WT”).

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 10 mL kanamycin (50 mg/mL) and spectinomycin (100 mg/mL) stocks, filter‑sterilize, aliquot and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 g kanamycin in 10 mL water (50 mg/mL).
Filter through 0.2 µm syringe filter, aliquot 1 mL, freeze at –20 °C.
Dissolve 1 g spectinomycin in 10 mL water (100 mg/mL).
Filter, aliquot 1 mL, freeze at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 25× M salts solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve anhydrous salts to give final 25× concentrations, adjust for hydration, bring to 1 L.

substeps.instruction: Add 88.7 g Na2HPO4 (0.625 M), 85.1 g KH2PO4 (0.625 M), 66.9 g NH4Cl (1.25 M), 17.8 g Na2SO4 (0.125 M) to ~900 mL water in a 2 L beaker.
Stir until dissolved, then bring volume to 1 L.
Store at room temperature; adjust weights if using hydrated salts.

steps.title: Prepare 5,000× trace metal stock
steps.instruction: Make individual 30 mL metal stocks, autoclave (except FeCl3), combine into a 50 mL mixed trace metal solution.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 8.82 g MnCl2·4H2O (10 mM), 5.93 g ZnSO4·7H2O (2 M), 8.62 g CoCl2·6H2O (2 mM), 0.807 g CuCl2 (2 mM), 0.777 g NiCl2 (2 mM), 1.03 g Na2SeO3 (2 mM), 1.45 g Na2MoO4·2H2O (2 mM), 0.371 g H3BO3 (2 mM) in 30 mL Milli‑Q water each.
Autoclave each metal solution separately.
Dissolve 8.62 g FeCl3 in 0.1 M HCl to 30 mL, filter (0.2 µm) – do NOT autoclave.
Combine 500 µL of each metal stock (except FeCl3) with 25 µL of the FeCl3 stock in 20.5 mL sterile water; add 25 µL FeCl3 solution to reach total 50 mL.
Store at 15–25 °C; minor precipitation is acceptable.

steps.title: Prepare 50× 5052 solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve glucose, lactose, and glycerol in warm water, bring to 500 mL, autoclave.

substeps.instruction: Add 12.5 g α‑D‑glucose (25 mg/mL), 50 g α‑lactose (100 mg/mL), and 125 mL glycerol (25 % v/v) to ~300 mL warm water in a 0.5 L beaker.
Stir until fully dissolved (microwave heating may be needed; remove stir bar before microwaving).
Add water to 500 mL total volume.
Autoclave on liquid cycle.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM Tet2‑Et solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve Tet2‑Et in DMF to 100 mM (8.5 mg in 275 µL total), vortex, store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 8.5 mg Tet2‑Et to 275 µL DMF, vortex until dissolved.
Aliquot as needed, store at –20 °C; vortex again after freeze‑thaw.

steps.title: Prepare ZY media (1 L batch)
steps.instruction: Combine tryptone, yeast extract, water, autoclave, and store.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract to ~900 mL water in a 1 L beaker.
Stir, then bring volume to 1 L.
Autoclave for sterilization.

steps.title: Prepare ZY‑NIM and ZY‑AIM (50 mL each)
steps.instruction: Dilute concentrated stocks into ZY media, add antibiotics, and keep sterile.

substeps.instruction: For each 50 mL batch, combine 47 mL ZY media, 0.1 mL MgSO4 (1 M), 2 mL 25× M salts, 1 mL 50× 5052, and 0.625 mL 40 % glucose (for NIM only).
Add 10 µL trace metal stock to each.
For BL21(DE3) add 100 µg/mL spectinomycin and 50 µg/mL kanamycin; for B95(DE3) add 50 µg/mL spectinomycin and 25 µg/mL kanamycin.
Prepare immediately before use; keep sterile.

steps.title: Prepare defined NIM and AIM media (optional)
steps.instruction: Make Aspartate 5 % (w/v) solution and 18‑amino‑acid 25× mix, then assemble NIM/AIM as described.

substeps.instruction: Aspartate: dissolve 50 g L‑aspartic acid in 900 mL water, adjust pH to 7.5 with 8 M NaOH, bring to 1 L, autoclave.

18‑amino‑acid 25×: dissolve 5 g each of the 18 amino acids in 800 mL water, stir (warm if needed) for several hours, bring to 1 L, filter‑sterilize, aliquot 45 mL into 50 mL conicals, store at –20 °C.

Assemble NIM/AIM (50 mL) by adding 2.5 mL Aspartate, 1 mL 50× 5052, 2 mL 18‑aa mix, 2 mL 25× M salts, 100 µL 1 M MgSO4, 6.25 mL 40 % glucose (NIM only), 10 µL trace metal, and sterile water to 50 mL; add antibiotics as above.

steps.title: Day 1 – Transform plasmids into competent cells
steps.instruction: Co‑transform pAJE3‑E7 with either pET28‑sfGFP WT or pET28‑sfGFP 150 into chemically competent BL21(DE3) or B95(DE3) cells.

substeps.instruction: Label two 1.7 mL Eppendorf tubes for each expression.
Add 1 µL pAJE plasmid (~200–400 ng) and 2 µL pET28‑sfGFP plasmid (~100 ng) to each tube, keep on ice 5 min.
Thaw 50 µL competent cells on ice, add to each tube, mix gently, incubate on ice 30 min.
Heat‑shock at 42 °C for exactly 45 s, return to ice 2 min.
Add 1 mL SOC, recover at 37 °C, shaking >200 rpm: 90 min for BL21(DE3), 120 min for B95(DE3).
Centrifuge tubes 3 000 × g 3 min, discard 900 µL supernatant, resuspend pellet in remaining 100 µL, spread entire 100 µL on LB/agar plate with appropriate antibiotics.
Dry plates with lid ajar ~20 min near flame, incubate upside‑down overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Day 2 – Inoculate non‑inducing starter cultures
steps.instruction: Pick colonies from plates, inoculate 5 mL NIM (or ZY‑NIM) starter cultures, grow overnight.

substeps.instruction: Label two 15 mL sterile culture tubes: “pAJE3‑E7 + sfGFP WT” and “pAJE3‑E7 + sfGFP 150”.
Add 5 mL NIM (or ZY‑NIM) to each tube.
Scrape several dozen colonies from the corresponding plate with a sterile tip, transfer to the tube, break up clumps by gentle pipetting; culture should appear slightly turbid.
Incubate at 37 °C, shaking 250 rpm, overnight (~12–18 h).

steps.title: Day 3 – Set up auto‑induction expression cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate 50 mL AIM cultures to OD600 ≈ 0.05, add Tet2‑Et or DMF, antifoam, and grow 20–24 h.

substeps.instruction: Measure OD600 of overnight starter cultures; calculate volume to achieve OD600 0.05 in 50 mL (e.g., if OD600 = 5, add 0.5 mL starter to 49.5 mL media).
Prepare three 50 mL AIM flasks: (i) sfGFP WT (no ncAA), (ii) sfGFP 150 + Tet2‑Et, (iii) sfGFP 150 + DMF control.
For Tet2‑Et cultures add 250 µL of 100 mM Tet2‑Et stock (final 0.5 mM). For control cultures add 250 µL pure DMF.
Add antifoam B (≈2 drops ≈50 µL) per 50 mL flask (for 1 L cultures use ~6 drops ≈150 µL).
Incubate at 37 °C, 250 rpm, 20–24 h. If lower temperature expression is needed, monitor OD600; when OD600 ≈ 1.5 shift to desired temperature and continue 16–24 h.

steps.title: Day 4 – Measure fluorescence, harvest cells
steps.instruction: Record OD600 and sfGFP fluorescence, centrifuge cultures, resuspend pellets in lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Measure OD600 of each 50 mL culture.
Measure sfGFP fluorescence (ex 485 nm/em 510 nm); WT should be green, Tet2‑Et culture orange, DMF control minimal.
Centrifuge at 5 000–10 000 × g, 10–20 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 10 % (v/v) glycerol, 5 mM imidazole (avoid DTT or β‑mercaptoethanol).
Aliquot or flash‑freeze in liquid N2 and store at –80 °C, or proceed to purification.

steps.title: Purify His‑tagged Tet2‑protein
steps.instruction: Bind clarified lysate to TALON resin, wash, elute with imidazole, keep reducing agents out.

substeps.instruction: Lyse cells (e.g., sonication or French press) in the same Tris/NaCl/glycerol/imidazole buffer.
Clarify lysate by centrifugation 15 000 × g, 30 min, 4 °C.
Equilibrate TALON resin with binding buffer (same composition).
Incubate clarified lysate with resin (e.g., 500 µL resin per 50 mL culture) for 30 min at 4 °C with gentle mixing.
Pack resin in column, wash with 10 column volumes binding buffer.
Elute protein with buffer containing 250 mM imidazole.
Collect eluate, keep on ice; do not add DTT or β‑mercaptoethanol.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration by A280
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 280 nm and calculate concentration using appropriate extinction coefficients.

substeps.instruction: Record A280 of purified protein (path length 1 cm).
For sfGFP WT use ε280 = 24 080 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹; for sfGFP‑Tet2‑Et use ε280 = 37 640 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹.
Apply Beer’s law: c = A280 / (ε × 1 cm). Example: A280 = 1.8 → 76 µM WT or 48 µM Tet2‑Et.

steps.title: Assess Tet2 reactivity with sTCO‑PEG 5000
steps.instruction: Conjugate protein to sTCO‑PEG 5000, run SDS‑PAGE, and evaluate mobility shift.

substeps.instruction: Mix purified protein (≈2 µg per lane) with a 10‑fold molar excess of sTCO‑PEG 5000 in suitable buffer; incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Add SDS sample buffer, boil 5 min, load 10–15 µL (≈2 µg) onto a 12 % SDS‑PAGE gel.
Run gel for ~1 h, stain with Coomassie.
Compare migration of Tet2‑protein (+PEG shift) to WT control; quantify shift by densitometry if desired.
